prompt: A frame moving with constant velocity relative to an inertial frame is:
options: Inertial only if the speed is small
Inertial only if it is at rest
explain: Frames with constant relative velocity (no acceleration) are all inertial; Newton's laws hold in each.
subject: Physics

prompt: Pseudo (fictitious) force has to be introduced when working in a frame that is:
options: At rest relative to the ground
Accelerated relative to an inertial frame
explain: Pseudo force appears only in non-inertial (accelerated or rotating) frames.
subject: Physics

prompt: On shifting the origin of the coordinate system, which quantity remains unchanged?
explain: Positions change with the origin, but Δr = r₂ − r₁ is the same since both shift equally.
subject: Physics

prompt: A particle goes along a semicircle of radius R. Displacement : distance =
explain: Displacement = diameter = 2R; distance = πR; ratio 2 : π.
subject: Physics

prompt: Displacement of a particle between two instants depends on:
options: Only the initial and final positions
The time taken for the motion
explain: Displacement is path-independent; it is the vector from initial to final position.
subject: Physics

prompt: A particle moves from A to B and back to A along the same path. What is its average velocity over the whole trip?
explain: Net displacement is zero for a round trip, so average velocity is zero, while average speed is non-zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: Instantaneous velocity of a particle is defined as:
explain: Instantaneous velocity is the limit of average velocity as Δt→0, i.e. the derivative dx/dt.
subject: Physics

prompt: On an x–t graph, the slope of the chord joining two points gives:
explain: The chord slope is Δx/Δt, the average velocity. The tangent slope is the instantaneous velocity.
subject: Physics

prompt: The slope of a distance–time graph of a moving particle can never be:
explain: Distance never decreases, so the slope (speed) is ≥ 0. Zero slope means rest.
subject: Physics

prompt: Average speed equals the magnitude of average velocity only when motion is:
options: Along a straight line without reversal
In a circle at constant speed
explain: Distance equals the displacement magnitude only if there is no change of direction along a line.
subject: Physics

prompt: Speed v on a circle. Magnitude of average velocity in half a revolution is:
explain: Displacement 2R, time πR/v, so the average velocity magnitude is 2v/π.
subject: Physics

prompt: The relation v_avg = (u + v)/2 is valid only when:
options: Speed is constant in a circle
Motion is in any straight line
explain: The simple mean of initial and final velocity gives the average velocity only for uniform (constant) acceleration.
subject: Physics

prompt: If x = A + Bt + Ct², the velocity of the particle at t = 0 is:
explain: v = dx/dt = B + 2Ct, so v(0) = B.
subject: Physics

prompt: Instantaneous speed compared with the magnitude of instantaneous velocity is:
explain: Speed is |v| at every instant. Only average speed and average velocity can differ.
subject: Physics

prompt: The instantaneous velocity of a particle on a curved path is directed:
options: Along the tangent to the path
explain: As Δt→0 the displacement lies along the tangent to the path.
subject: Physics

prompt: An x–t graph is a straight line parallel to the time axis. The particle is:
explain: Zero slope means dx/dt = 0, so the particle is at rest at a fixed position.
subject: Physics

prompt: In 1-D motion, a negative velocity means the particle:
options: Moves opposite to the chosen positive direction
explain: The sign of velocity only gives direction. Speed is always non-negative.
subject: Physics

prompt: If x ∝ t², the instantaneous velocity of the particle is proportional to:
explain: v = dx/dt ∝ 2t, so v ∝ t.
subject: Physics

prompt: The area under a speed–time graph over an interval gives:
explain: Speed is non-negative, so the area is the total path length (distance). Area under a v–t graph is displacement.
subject: Physics

prompt: For motion along a line, the magnitude of average velocity over an interval is never greater than:
explain: Displacement ≤ distance, so |v_avg| ≤ average speed, with equality for motion without reversal.
subject: Physics

prompt: A car covers half the distance at speed v₁ and the other half at v₂. Its average speed is:
explain: Equal distances give the harmonic mean: 2v₁v₂/(v₁+v₂).
subject: Physics

prompt: A body moves with speed v₁ for half the time and v₂ for the other half. Average speed equals:
explain: For equal time intervals, average speed is the arithmetic mean.
subject: Physics

prompt: A particle's x–t graph is a curve, not a straight line. The motion is:
explain: The x–t slope is velocity. A changing slope means changing velocity.
subject: Physics

prompt: A particle moves in a circle with constant speed. Its velocity is:
explain: Velocity is a vector. Its direction changes, so the motion is non-uniform and accelerated.
subject: Physics

prompt: A particle returns to its starting point after time T. Its average velocity is:
explain: Net displacement is zero, so average velocity is zero. Average speed is not zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: Net signed area under a v–t graph between t₁ and t₂ gives the:
explain: ∫v dt is displacement. Area below the axis counts as negative.
subject: Physics

prompt: Instantaneous velocity at time t from an x–t graph is the:
options: Slope of the chord from t = 0
Slope of the tangent at t
Area under the graph up to t
Value of x divided by t
explain: v = dx/dt is the slope of the tangent to the x–t curve at that instant.
subject: Physics

prompt: The magnitude of average velocity equals average speed only if the motion is:
options: Along a straight line without reversing
explain: Distance equals the magnitude of displacement only for straight-line motion without reversal.
subject: Physics

prompt: A ball thrown vertically up is at its highest point. Its velocity and acceleration are:
explain: At the top v = 0 but a = g downward, so the motion is non-uniform.
subject: Physics

prompt: Same braking deceleration; initial speed doubled. Stopping distance becomes
explain: With v = 0, s = u²/2a, so s ∝ u². Doubling u gives 4s.
subject: Physics

prompt: Maximum height reached by a body projected vertically up with speed u (no air resistance)
explain: At the top v = 0, so 0 = u² − 2gH and H = u²/2g.
subject: Physics

prompt: Time of flight of a body thrown vertically up with speed u and returning to the same point
explain: Ascent time u/g plus equal descent time gives 2u/g.
subject: Physics

prompt: For constant nonzero acceleration, the position–time graph is
explain: x is quadratic in t, so the x–t graph is a parabola.
subject: Physics

prompt: A body decelerating uniformly to rest covers how much distance in its last second?
explain: By reversing the motion, s = ½a(1)² = a/2.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two bodies are freely falling under gravity. Their relative acceleration is
explain: Both have acceleration g downward, so the relative acceleration is zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: At the highest point of a vertical throw, the acceleration of the body is
explain: Velocity is momentarily zero but gravity still gives g downward.
subject: Physics

prompt: A ball thrown up with speed u from a tower vs one thrown down with u: speeds on reaching the ground
explain: The up-thrown ball returns to the tower top with speed u downward, so both hit with √(u² + 2gh).
subject: Physics

prompt: Launch speed of a vertical throw is doubled. Maximum height becomes
explain: H ∝ u², so doubling u gives 4 times the height.
subject: Physics

prompt: In vertical motion without air resistance, time of ascent compared with time of descent (same levels) is
explain: Motion is symmetric, so both times are u/g.
subject: Physics

prompt: The equations v = u + at, s = ut + ½at² and v² = u² + 2as hold only if
explain: They are derived assuming constant acceleration along a straight line.
subject: Physics

prompt: Total distance travelled by a ball thrown up with speed u until it returns to the start
explain: Distance is up + down = 2 × u²/2g = u²/g, while displacement is zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: Time to fall from rest through height 4h compared with time for height h
explain: t ∝ √h, so quadrupling h doubles t.
subject: Physics

prompt: In a velocity–time graph, the acceleration and displacement are given respectively by
explain: The slope of the v–t graph is a and the area under it is displacement.
subject: Physics

prompt: Uniform acceleration, speed u to v. Speed at the midpoint of the DISTANCE covered is
explain: Using v² = u² + 2as over s/2 and s gives v_mid² = (u² + v²)/2.
subject: Physics

prompt: A ball thrown vertically up passes the same height going up and coming down. Its velocities there are
options: Equal in magnitude, opposite in direction
explain: v² = u² − 2gh is the same at both passes, so the speeds are equal and the directions are opposite.
subject: Physics

prompt: In uniform acceleration a, displacements in successive equal intervals T differ by:
explain: s₂ − s₁ = aT² for any two consecutive equal time intervals T.
subject: Physics

prompt: From rest with uniform acceleration, times to cover 1st, 2nd, 3rd equal successive distances are in ratio:
explain: t ∝ √s, so the time for the nth equal segment is ∝ √n − √(n−1).
subject: Physics

prompt: Total distance travelled from a v–t graph equals:
options: Net signed area under the graph
Sum of areas taken without sign
Area of the largest portion only
explain: Distance uses |v|, so areas below the axis are added as positive; net signed area gives displacement.
subject: Physics

prompt: An x–t graph is a horizontal line (parallel to t-axis). The particle is:
options: Moving with zero speed only at t = 0
explain: Slope = 0, so v = 0 at all times; the position stays constant.
subject: Physics

prompt: At the peak (maximum) of an x–t curve, the particle's:
options: Velocity is zero and it reverses direction
Speed is a minimum non-zero value
explain: Slope of x–t is zero at a turning point, so v = 0 and the sign of v changes.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two particles' x–t graphs intersect at a point. This means they have the same:
explain: Intersection means equal x at equal t, so the particles meet. Their velocities need not be equal.
subject: Physics

prompt: Average velocity between two instants on an x–t graph is the slope of:
options: The chord joining the two points
The tangent at the later point
The line from the origin to the later point
explain: Δx/Δt is the slope of the chord. The tangent slope gives instantaneous velocity.
subject: Physics

prompt: A v–t graph cuts the time axis going from positive to negative. At that instant the particle:
options: Is momentarily at rest and reverses direction
explain: v changes sign through zero, so the direction of motion reverses at that instant.
subject: Physics

prompt: The part of a v–t graph lying below the time axis contributes what to displacement?
explain: v < 0 means motion in the negative direction, so that area is negative.
subject: Physics

prompt: A v–t graph is a horizontal straight line. The particle has:
explain: Slope of v–t is zero, so a = 0 and v is constant (not necessarily zero).
subject: Physics

prompt: A body speeds up uniformly from rest to v, then slows uniformly to rest, in total time T. Distance covered?
explain: The v–t graph is a triangle with base T and height v, so area = ½vT.
subject: Physics

prompt: Why can an x–t graph never contain a vertical segment?
options: The particle would be at two places at once
explain: A vertical segment means many positions at one instant, i.e. infinite velocity, which is physically impossible.
subject: Physics

prompt: A ball is thrown vertically up (up positive). Its x–t graph up to return is:
explain: x = ut − ½gt² has a negative t² coefficient, so the parabola opens downward with its vertex at the top.
subject: Physics

prompt: An x–t curve with a positive slope that keeps increasing (concave up) shows:
explain: Slope is v, so increasing slope means dv/dt > 0, i.e. positive acceleration (d²x/dt² > 0).
subject: Physics

prompt: Average acceleration over an interval on a v–t graph is the slope of:
options: The tangent at the end point
explain: Δv/Δt is the chord slope; the tangent slope gives instantaneous acceleration.
subject: Physics

prompt: An x–t graph is falling and getting steeper with time. The particle is:
explain: Velocity is negative and its magnitude grows, so v decreases and a is negative.
subject: Physics

prompt: In a v–t graph, area above the axis equals area below it. The net displacement is:
explain: The signed areas cancel, so displacement and average velocity are zero, but distance is not.
subject: Physics

prompt: A v–t graph is curved upward (slope increasing with time). This indicates:
explain: Slope of v–t is a, so a rising slope means a increases with time (non-uniform acceleration).
subject: Physics

prompt: Of two straight lines on an x–t graph, the one making a larger angle with the t-axis shows:
explain: A steeper line means a larger |slope|, so greater speed. Both lines have zero acceleration.
subject: Physics

prompt: Which of these physical quantities is a scalar even though it is shown with an arrow in circuits?
explain: Current adds algebraically, not by the vector law, so it is a scalar. Current density is a vector.
subject: Physics

prompt: A force F has components that sum to F. A unit vector Â = A/|A| has what dimensions?
explain: Â is the vector divided by its own magnitude, so it is dimensionless with magnitude 1.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two vectors of equal magnitude A act at 120°. What is the magnitude of the resultant?
explain: R² = 2A² + 2A²cos120° = A², so R = A.
subject: Physics

prompt: Which magnitude can NOT be the resultant of a 3 N and a 5 N vector?
explain: The resultant lies between 5−3 = 2 N and 5+3 = 8 N, so 1 N is impossible.
subject: Physics

prompt: Which set of three forces (in N) can keep a particle in equilibrium?
explain: For zero resultant, each force must lie between the difference and sum of the other two. Only 3, 4, 5 satisfies this.
subject: Physics

prompt: For a vector making angles α, β, γ with the x, y, z axes, what is cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ?
explain: The direction cosines l, m, n of any vector satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two equal vectors of magnitude A are inclined at 60°. What is the magnitude of their difference?
explain: |A−B| = 2A sin30° = A.
subject: Physics

prompt: If |A + B| = |A − B| for non-zero vectors, what is the angle between A and B?
explain: The condition requires AB cosθ = 0, so cosθ = 0 and θ = 90°.
subject: Physics

prompt: What is the unit vector along 3î + 4ĵ?
explain: The magnitude is √(9+16) = 5, so divide the vector by 5.
subject: Physics

prompt: What is the direction of a null vector?
explain: A null vector has zero magnitude, so no definite direction can be assigned to it.
subject: Physics

prompt: Three vectors are represented by the three sides of a triangle taken in the same order. What is their sum?
explain: By the triangle law, sides taken in the same order form a closed polygon, so the sum is the null vector.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two equal-magnitude vectors are inclined at angle θ. At what angle does the resultant lie from either vector?
explain: For P = Q, tanα = sinθ/(1+cosθ) = tan(θ/2). The resultant bisects the angle.
subject: Physics

prompt: Which of these quantities is a vector?
explain: Current density has a definite direction and obeys the vector law. The others are scalars.
subject: Physics

prompt: Why is a finite angular displacement NOT a vector?
explain: Finite rotations about different axes depend on order, so they fail commutative vector addition.
subject: Physics

prompt: A vector of magnitude 5 has one perpendicular component of 3. What is the other component?
subject: Physics

prompt: What does a vector A look like when multiplied by a negative scalar −k?
explain: A negative scalar scales the magnitude by k and reverses the direction.
subject: Physics

prompt: For perpendicular unit vectors, which result is correct?
explain: Cyclic order î→ĵ→k̂→î gives +. ĵ×k̂ = î. The others are in the reverse order, so they are negative.
subject: Physics

prompt: For vectors A and B, the magnitude of the resultant is maximum when the angle between them is:
explain: R is maximum (A + B) when cosθ = 1, i.e. θ = 0°, for parallel vectors.
subject: Physics

prompt: Which cannot be the magnitude of the resultant of a 4 N and a 7 N force?
explain: R lies between 7−4 = 3 N and 7+4 = 11 N, so 2 N is impossible.
subject: Physics

prompt: If |A + B| = |A − B| for non-zero vectors, the angle between A and B is:
explain: Equating the squares gives 4A·B = 0, so the vectors are perpendicular.
subject: Physics

prompt: For the sum of two equal-magnitude vectors, the resultant's direction is:
options: Along the bisector of the angle
explain: The parallelogram is a rhombus, so its diagonal bisects the angle between the sides.
subject: Physics

prompt: Electric current has magnitude and direction but is a scalar because it:
options: Does not obey vector addition laws
explain: Currents add algebraically at a junction, not by the triangle or parallelogram law.
subject: Physics

prompt: Finite rotations are not vectors mainly because they fail:
explain: Finite rotations about different axes give different results when the order is changed.
subject: Physics

prompt: If |A + B|² = |A|² + |B|², the angle between A and B is:
explain: The extra term 2AB cosθ must vanish, so cosθ = 0.
subject: Physics

prompt: Vectors A, B, C are represented by the three sides of a triangle taken in order. A + B + C equals:
explain: By the triangle law, the vector sum of sides taken in order around a closed figure is zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: For two vectors of equal magnitude A at angle θ, |A₁ − A₂| equals:
explain: √(2A² − 2A² cosθ) = 2A sin(θ/2). At 60° the difference equals A.
subject: Physics

prompt: Minimum number of coplanar vectors of unequal magnitudes that can give a zero resultant:
explain: Two unequal vectors cannot cancel. Three can, if they can form a triangle.
subject: Physics

prompt: |A + B| = |A| + |B| holds only when A and B are:
options: Equal in magnitude at any angle
explain: The resultant is maximum at θ = 0°, where the magnitudes simply add.
subject: Physics

prompt: Compared with A − B, the vector B − A has:
explain: B − A = −(A − B). Vector subtraction is not commutative.
subject: Physics

prompt: Three coplanar vectors of equal magnitude, inclined at 120° to each other, have resultant:
explain: They form a closed equilateral triangle, so the sum is zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: In a parallelogram with A and B as adjacent sides, the diagonal joining their tips represents:
explain: The diagonal through the common point is A + B. The other diagonal is the difference.
subject: Physics

prompt: A + B is perpendicular to A and |B| = 2|A|. The angle between A and B is:
explain: Resultant ⊥ A needs A + B cosθ = 0, so cosθ = −A/B = −1/2, giving θ = 120°.
subject: Physics

prompt: For any two vectors, |A + B|² + |A − B|² equals:
explain: Adding (A²+B²+2AB cosθ) and (A²+B²−2AB cosθ) cancels the cross terms, leaving 2(A²+B²).
subject: Physics

prompt: In the polygon law, the resultant of vectors placed head to tail is the side joining:
options: Tail of last to head of first
Head of first to head of last
Tail of first to head of last
explain: The closing side runs from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last.
subject: Physics

prompt: For two vectors of fixed magnitudes A and B, |A − B| is maximum when the angle between them is:
explain: cosθ = −1 at 180°, so |A − B| = A + B (maximum).
subject: Physics

prompt: For nonzero vectors A and B, if |A × B| = A·B, the angle between them is:
explain: AB sinθ = AB cosθ gives tanθ = 1, so θ = 45°.
subject: Physics

prompt: If |A + B| = |A − B| for nonzero vectors, the angle between A and B is:
explain: Equal magnitudes need A·B = 0, so the vectors are perpendicular.
subject: Physics

prompt: The value of A·(A × B) is:
explain: A × B is perpendicular to A, so the dot product is zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: The scalar triple product |A·(B × C)| gives the:
explain: |A·(B×C)| is the volume of the parallelepiped on A, B, C.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two vectors lie in the x–y plane. Their cross product points along:
explain: A × B is perpendicular to the plane of A and B, which is the z-axis here.
subject: Physics

prompt: The vector triple product A × (B × C) equals:
explain: BAC–CAB rule: A×(B×C) = B(A·C) − C(A·B). The cross product is not associative.
subject: Physics

prompt: Magnetic force F = q(v × B) does no work on a charge because:
explain: F ⟂ v gives F·v = 0, so the power and work are zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: The dot product A·B is negative when the angle between the vectors is:
explain: cosθ < 0 for 90° < θ ≤ 180°, so the dot product is negative there.
subject: Physics

prompt: Which of these physical quantities is a cross product of two vectors?
explain: L = r × p; power and work are dot products, KE is a scalar.
subject: Physics

prompt: For nonzero vectors, A × B = 0 means A and B are:
explain: sinθ = 0 gives θ = 0° or 180°.
subject: Physics

prompt: The torque on an electric dipole, τ = p × E, vanishes when the angle between p and E is:
explain: τ = pE sinθ = 0 for θ = 0° or 180°.
subject: Physics

prompt: The magnitude |A × B| represents geometrically the:
explain: A and B as adjacent sides of a parallelogram give area |A × B|.
subject: Physics

prompt: Which of these is NOT a dot product of two vectors?
explain: Torque = r × F is a cross product; W = F·s, P = F·v, φ = B·A are dot products.
subject: Physics

prompt: The value of A × A for any vector A is:
explain: sin 0° = 0, so A × A = 0 (a null vector, not scalar zero).
subject: Physics

prompt: Dot product of î·î and î·ĵ respectively are:
explain: Same unit vectors give 1; perpendicular ones give 0.
subject: Physics

prompt: Vectors A and B are perpendicular. Then which relation holds?
explain: θ = 90°: cosθ = 0, sinθ = 1.
subject: Physics

prompt: A·B = |A × B| in magnitude means tan θ equals:
explain: Equating cosθ and sinθ gives tanθ = 1 (θ = 45°).
subject: Physics

prompt: Two bodies in free fall near Earth (no air drag). Their relative acceleration is:
explain: Both have acceleration g, so a_A − a_B = 0 and relative velocity stays constant.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two balls are in flight under gravity only. Their separation vs time graph is:
explain: Relative acceleration is zero, so relative velocity is constant and separation changes linearly with t.
subject: Physics

prompt: The slope of the (x_A − x_B) versus time graph gives:
explain: d(x_A − x_B)/dt = v_A − v_B = v_AB.
subject: Physics

prompt: Ball A is thrown up at speed u from ground; ball B is dropped from height h at the same instant. They meet after:
explain: Relative acceleration is zero; relative speed is u, so t = h/u.
subject: Physics

prompt: If v_AB = 0 for two bodies on a line, their separation:
explain: Equal velocities mean no relative motion, so the gap stays constant.
subject: Physics

prompt: Along +x, A moves at +20 m/s and B at −30 m/s. The magnitude of v_AB is:
explain: v_AB = 20 − (−30) = 50 m/s. Opposite directions: speeds add.
subject: Physics

prompt: A is dropped; B is dropped Δt later. While both fall, v_AB is:
explain: Same acceleration g, so v_A − v_B = g(t) − g(t−Δt) = gΔt, constant.
subject: Physics

prompt: On velocity–time graphs of two bodies, the intersection point means:
options: They have the same velocity then
explain: v–t crossing means v_A = v_B (v_rel = 0), not necessarily the same position.
subject: Physics

prompt: From one point, one ball is thrown up and another down, both at speed u. Their relative velocity in flight:
explain: Both have acceleration g, so v_rel stays at u − (−u) = 2u.
subject: Physics

prompt: A lift rises at constant speed v. A bolt falls from its ceiling, height h. Time to hit the floor:
explain: In the lift frame (inertial), the bolt starts at rest with acceleration g, so t = √(2h/g).
subject: Physics

prompt: A car starts from rest with uniform acceleration behind a truck moving at constant speed. Separation is extreme when:
options: The car's velocity is double the truck's
explain: Separation is stationary (d(Δx)/dt = 0) when the relative velocity is zero, i.e. the velocities are equal.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two frames move with constant relative velocity. A body's accelerations measured in them are:
options: Differ by the relative speed ÷ time
explain: The relative acceleration of the frames is zero, so a' = a. This is Galilean invariance of acceleration.
subject: Physics

prompt: For a projectile landing at launch level, max height H and time of flight T are related by:
explain: H = u²sin²α/2g and T = 2u sinα/g, so H = g(T/2)²/2 = gT²/8.
subject: Physics

prompt: Same speed, angles α and (90° − α). Ratio of times of flight T₁/T₂ is:
explain: T ∝ sinα, and sinα/sin(90°−α) = sinα/cosα = tanα.
subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight

prompt: Trajectory equation of a projectile in terms of its range R and launch angle α:
explain: From y = x tanα − gx²/(2u²cos²α), using R = 2u²sinα cosα/g.
subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight

prompt: A projectile of mass m is launched at α with speed u and lands at the same level. Change in momentum is:
explain: Horizontal momentum is unchanged; vertical goes from +mu sinα to −mu sinα, so Δp = 2mu sinα downward.
subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight

prompt: For a projectile (same level landing), R = 4H cotα. What is R for α with tanα = 1/2 in terms of H?
explain: R/H = 4/tanα = 4×2 = 8, so R = 8H.
subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight

prompt: Radius of curvature at the highest point of a projectile launched at angle α with speed u:
explain: At the top, velocity is u cosα and g is wholly centripetal, so r = u²cos²α/g.
subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight

prompt: A particle moves uniformly with speed v on a circle. Magnitude of change in velocity in half a revolution?
explain: Velocity reverses: Δv = v − (−v) = 2v.
subject: Physics

prompt: Speed v, angular displacement θ in uniform circular motion. Magnitude of change in velocity is
explain: Chord of the velocity-vector triangle gives |Δv| = 2v sin(θ/2).
subject: Physics

prompt: Centripetal acceleration in terms of radius r and time period T is
explain: a = ω²r with ω = 2π/T gives 4π²r/T².
subject: Physics

prompt: Work done by the centripetal force in uniform circular motion is
explain: Force is always perpendicular to displacement, so work is zero always.
subject: Physics

prompt: For a particle in uniform circular motion, the average velocity over one full revolution is
explain: Net displacement over a full revolution is zero, so average velocity is zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: The angular velocity vector of a particle in circular motion is directed
options: Along the axis, by right-hand rule
explain: ω is an axial vector along the rotation axis, fixed by the right-hand rule.
subject: Physics

prompt: At constant speed, the graph of centripetal acceleration versus radius r is a
explain: a ∝ 1/r at constant v gives a rectangular hyperbola.
subject: Physics

prompt: Angular velocity of the second hand of a clock is
explain: One revolution (2π) in 60 s gives ω = 2π/60 = π/30 rad/s.
subject: Physics

prompt: Centripetal acceleration of a particle in a circle of radius r with frequency n is
explain: ω = 2πn, so a = ω²r = 4π²n²r.
subject: Physics

prompt: At constant angular velocity, the graph of centripetal acceleration versus radius r is
explain: With ω fixed, a ∝ r, so the graph is a straight line through the origin.
subject: Physics

prompt: In uniform circular motion, the average acceleration over one complete revolution is
explain: Average acceleration = Δv/T, and Δv = 0 after a full turn, so it is zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: In uniform circular motion, the angle between velocity and angular velocity vectors is
